source.text: Τῇ δὲ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ ἔρχεται πρωῒ σκοτίας ἔτι οὔσης εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον, καὶ βλέπει τὸν λίθον ἠρμένον ἐκ τοῦ μνημείου.

records.literal_gloss: On the now first [day] of the sabbaths Mary the Magdalene comes early, darkness still being, to the tomb, and sees the stone having been taken away from the tomb.

en.L: Now on the first [day] of the week Mary Magdalene comes to the tomb early, while it was still dark, and sees the stone taken away from the tomb.
en.B: On the first day of the week Mary Magdalene came to the tomb in the early morning, while it was still dark, and found that the stone had been taken away from it.
en.R: It was the first day of the week, very early, and it was still dark. Mary Magdalene made her way to the tomb, and she saw that the stone had been moved away from it.

es.L: El primer [día] de la semana, María Magdalena viene temprano al sepulcro, cuando todavía estaba oscuro, y ve la piedra quitada del sepulcro.
es.B: El primer día de la semana, muy de madrugada, cuando todavía estaba oscuro, María Magdalena fue al sepulcro y encontró que la piedra había sido quitada de allí.
es.R: Era el primer día de la semana, muy temprano, y todavía estaba oscuro. María Magdalena fue a la tumba y vio que habían quitado la piedra.

fr.L: Or le premier [jour] de la semaine, Marie de Magdala vient au tombeau de bon matin, alors qu’il faisait encore sombre, et elle voit la pierre enlevée du tombeau.
fr.B: Le premier jour de la semaine, Marie de Magdala se rendit au tombeau de grand matin, alors qu’il faisait encore nuit, et elle vit que la pierre avait été enlevée du tombeau.
fr.R: C’était le premier jour de la semaine, très tôt le matin, et il faisait encore nuit. Marie de Magdala est allée au tombeau, et elle a vu que la pierre avait été déplacée.

sw.L: Basi, siku ya kwanza ya juma, Mariamu Magdalene anakuja kaburini mapema, giza likiwa bado lipo, naye anaona jiwe limeinuliwa kutoka kaburini.
sw.B: Siku ya kwanza ya juma, Mariamu Magdalene alifika kaburini mapema asubuhi, wakati bado kulikuwa na giza, akakuta jiwe limekwisha kuondoshwa kaburini.
sw.R: Ilikuwa siku ya kwanza ya juma, asubuhi na mapema sana, na bado kulikuwa na giza. Mariamu Magdalene alikwenda kaburini, akaona kwamba jiwe lilikuwa limesogezwa mbali na kaburi.

vi.L: Vào ngày thứ nhất trong tuần, Ma-ri Ma-đơ-len đến mộ lúc sáng sớm, khi trời còn tối, và thấy tảng đá đã được dời khỏi mộ.
vi.B: Vào ngày thứ nhất trong tuần, lúc trời còn tối, Ma-ri Ma-đơ-len đến mộ từ sáng sớm và thấy tảng đá đã bị dời khỏi mộ.
vi.R: Hôm ấy là ngày đầu tuần, trời còn rất sớm và vẫn còn tối. Ma-ri Ma-đơ-len đi đến mộ, và bà thấy tảng đá đã bị dời ra khỏi mộ.

ko.L: 그런데 주간의 첫 [날], 막달라 마리아가 아직 어두울 때 이른 아침에 무덤으로 온다. 그리고 돌이 무덤에서 옮겨져 있는 것을 본다.
ko.B: 주간의 첫날 이른 아침, 아직 어두울 때에 막달라 마리아가 무덤에 왔다. 그리고 무덤에서 돌이 치워져 있는 것을 보았다.
ko.R: 일주일의 첫날, 아주 이른 아침이었다. 아직 어두웠다. 막달라 마리아가 무덤으로 갔다. 그런데 무덤을 막고 있던 돌이 치워져 있었다.

pt.L: E no primeiro [dia] da semana Maria Madalena vem ao túmulo de madrugada, estando ainda escuro, e vê a pedra retirada do túmulo.
pt.B: No primeiro dia da semana, Maria Madalena foi ao túmulo de madrugada, quando ainda estava escuro, e viu que a pedra tinha sido retirada da entrada.
pt.R: Era o primeiro dia da semana, bem cedo, e ainda estava escuro. Maria Madalena foi até o túmulo e viu que a pedra tinha sido tirada da entrada.

am.L: ከሳምንቱም በመጀመሪያው [ቀን] መግደላዊት ማርያም ገና ጨለማ ሳለ ማልዳ ወደ መቃብሩ ትመጣለች፤ ድንጋዩም ከመቃብሩ ተነሥቶ ታያለች።
am.B: በሳምንቱ የመጀመሪያ ቀን መግደላዊት ማርያም ገና ጨለማ ሳለ በማለዳ ወደ መቃብሩ መጣች፤ ድንጋዩም ከመቃብሩ ላይ ተነሥቶ አገኘች።
am.R: የሳምንቱ የመጀመሪያ ቀን ነበረ። ገና በጣም ማለዳ ነበር፤ ጨለማም ነበረ። መግደላዊት ማርያም ወደ መቃብሩ ሄደች፤ ድንጋዩም ከመቃብሩ ላይ ተነሥቶ አየች።

decisions.choice: the first of the sabbaths: the first day of the week, the day after the Sabbath
decisions.reason: The plural of the word for Sabbath was also used for the week, and "the first" means its first day. It is the day we call Sunday. Jesus had been buried in haste on the Friday, the day of Preparation, before the Sabbath began (19:31, 42), and nothing could be done on the Sabbath itself. Mary comes as soon as the Sabbath is over. The same phrase opens the evening scene in verse 19.

decisions.choice: Mary Magdalene: Mary from Magdala
decisions.reason: Magdala was a town on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee. John has already named her among the women standing near the cross (19:25). Luke says that she had followed Jesus from Galilee after he set her free from seven demons (Luke 8:2). Nothing in the Gospels makes her the sinful woman of Luke 7:36-50.

decisions.choice: early, while it was still dark: before dawn
decisions.reason: πρωῒ is the last part of the night, before sunrise (Mark 13:35 uses it for the last watch). John adds that it was still dark. The other Gospels speak of the women coming as the sun rose (Mark 16:2); the details fit a walk that began in the dark and ended at first light.

decisions.choice: sees the stone taken away: she sees that it has been moved, not who moved it
alternatives: sees the stone being taken away
decisions.reason: The participle is passive and in the perfect: the stone has been lifted away and is no longer in place. Mary sees the result and draws her own conclusion in verse 2. A stone closed the opening of the tomb, as at Lazarus's tomb (11:38-39).

decisions.choice: comes, sees (L); came, found (B); made her way, saw (R)
decisions.reason: John tells much of this passage in the present tense, the historic present: she "comes" and "sees", she "runs", Peter "comes" and "sees", Jesus "says". It is a lively way of telling a story. Literal keeps the present so that readers see the Greek form; Balanced and Readable use the past, which is the normal tense for telling a story in English. This decision covers every historic present in 20:1-18.

decisions.choice: the first day of the week
decisions.reason: Every level keeps John's way of naming the day (meaning decision m1) rather than "Sunday", so that readers can see the link with verse 19.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (viene, ve); pretérito at Balanced and Readable (fue, encontró, vio)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John (11:7): Literal keeps John's present tense; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: sepulcro (L, B); tumba (R)
decisions.reason: As at Lazarus's tomb (11:31, 38): "sepulcro" at Literal and Balanced, the everyday "tumba" at Readable. Readable says "habían quitado" with no subject, so it does not say who moved the stone (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John's present tense ("elle vient", "elle voit", "elle court", "Jésus lui dit"); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for the passage (20:1-18), which John tells largely in the historic present. The passé simple ("se rendit", "vit") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Literal uses it for the Greek past tenses and keeps the present wherever John has it, as the English Literal does. Readable uses the passé composé ("elle est allée"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first.

decisions.choice: le premier jour de la semaine; Marie de Magdala
decisions.reason: Every level keeps John's way of naming the day rather than "dimanche", so that the link with verse 19 can be seen (meaning decision m1). "Marie de Magdala" says where she came from (meaning decision m2), as at 19:25; the traditional "Marie-Madeleine" hides it.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anakuja, anaona); past at Balanced and Readable (alifika, akakuta; alikwenda, akaona)
decisions.reason: John tells much of this passage in the present (she "comes", "sees", "runs"; Jesus "says"). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced tells the story in the narrative past, with -li- for the first verb and -ka- for those that follow, as written Swahili does, and Readable uses the plain past. This holds for the whole of 20:1-18.

decisions.choice: "đến", "thấy" with no past marker (L); past shown by context (B, R)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese verbs have no tense, so Literal keeps John's historic present (here and in 20:2, 20:5-6, 20:12-18) by leaving out "đã"; Balanced and Readable tell the story as past.

decisions.choice: "ngày thứ nhất trong tuần" (L, B); "ngày đầu tuần" (R)
decisions.reason: "Chủ Nhật" would name the later Christian day; John names the day by its place after the Sabbath.

decisions.choice: historic present "온다", "본다", "말한다" (L); past (B, R), through this passage
decisions.reason: Literal keeps John's present tense in narrative (20:1, 2, 5, 6, 12, 13, 15-18); Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past. One decision for 20:1-18.

decisions.choice: vem, vê (L); foi, viu (B, R)
decisions.reason: For this passage, as the English: Literal keeps John's historic present ("vem", "vê", "corre", "diz"); Balanced and Readable tell the story in the pretérito perfeito, the normal past of Portuguese narrative.

decisions.choice: da entrada
decisions.reason: Repeating "túmulo" in one short sentence is clumsy in Portuguese; "da entrada" says the same thing, since the stone closed the opening (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: መግደላዊት ማርያም (Mary Magdalene) at every level
alternatives: ከመቅደላ የሆነችው ማርያም (Mary from Magdala), used at Readable in Matthew 27:56
decisions.reason: She is known by this name in Amharic, and John uses it as a name; the meaning decision explains where she came from, so Readable keeps the name too.

source.text: τρέχει οὖν καὶ ἔρχεται πρὸς Σίμωνα Πέτρον καὶ πρὸς τὸν ἄλλον μαθητὴν ὃν ἐφίλει ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἦραν τὸν κύριον ἐκ τοῦ μνημείου, καὶ οὐκ οἴδαμεν ποῦ ἔθηκαν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Runs therefore and comes to Simon Peter and to the other disciple whom was loving the Jesus, and says to them, "They took the Lord out of the tomb, and not we know where they laid him."

en.L: So she runs and comes to Simon Peter and to the other disciple, whom Jesus loved, and says to them, "They have taken the Lord out of the tomb, and we do not know where they have laid {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.B: She ran off, then, to find Simon Peter and the other disciple, whom Jesus loved. "They have removed the Lord from the tomb," she told them, "and we do not know where they have laid {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.R: So she ran to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple too, the one whom Jesus loved. She told them, "Someone has taken the Lord away from the tomb! We do not know where they have put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

es.L: Corre, pues, y va [a ver] a Simón Pedro y al otro discípulo, al que Jesús amaba, y les dice: «Sacaron al Señor del sepulcro, y no sabemos dónde {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} pusieron».
es.B: Entonces salió corriendo a buscar a Simón Pedro y al otro discípulo, aquel a quien Jesús amaba. «Han sacado del sepulcro al Señor —les dijo—, y no sabemos dónde {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} han dejado».
es.R: Así que corrió a buscar a Simón Pedro y también al otro discípulo, el discípulo a quien Jesús amaba. Les dijo: «¡Alguien se llevó al Señor de la tumba! No sabemos dónde {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} pusieron».

fr.L: Elle court donc et vient vers Simon Pierre et vers l’autre disciple, que Jésus aimait, et elle leur dit : « Ils ont enlevé le Seigneur du tombeau, et nous ne savons pas où ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont déposé. »
fr.B: Elle partit donc en courant trouver Simon Pierre et l’autre disciple, celui que Jésus aimait. « On a enlevé le Seigneur du tombeau, leur dit-elle, et nous ne savons pas où on {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a déposé. »
fr.R: Alors elle a couru trouver Simon Pierre, et aussi l’autre disciple, celui que Jésus aimait. Elle leur a dit : « Quelqu’un a enlevé le Seigneur du tombeau ! Nous ne savons pas où on {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a mis. »

sw.L: Basi anakimbia, anakuja kwa Simoni Petro na kwa yule mwanafunzi mwingine ambaye Yesu alimpenda, na anawaambia, "Wamemchukua Bwana kutoka kaburini, nasi hatujui wamemweka wapi."
sw.B: Basi alikimbia kwenda kwa Simoni Petro na kwa yule mwanafunzi mwingine, ambaye Yesu alimpenda. "Wamemtoa Bwana kaburini," akawaambia, "nasi hatujui wamemweka wapi."
sw.R: Basi alikimbia kwa Simoni Petro, na pia kwa yule mwanafunzi mwingine, yule ambaye Yesu alimpenda. Akawaambia, "Mtu fulani amemchukua Bwana kutoka kaburini! Hatujui wamemweka wapi."

vi.L: Vậy bà chạy đến cùng Si-môn Phi-e-rơ và môn đồ kia, là người Đức Giê-xu yêu, và nói với họ: "Người ta đã đem Chúa ra khỏi mộ, và chúng tôi không biết họ đã đặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở đâu."
vi.B: Vậy bà chạy đi tìm Si-môn Phi-e-rơ và môn đồ kia, người mà Đức Giê-xu yêu. "Người ta đã đem Chúa ra khỏi mộ rồi," bà nói với họ, "và chúng tôi không biết họ đặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở đâu."
vi.R: Vậy bà chạy đến gặp Si-môn Phi-e-rơ và môn đồ kia, là người Đức Giê-xu yêu. Bà nói với họ: "Có người đã đem Chúa ra khỏi mộ rồi! Chúng tôi không biết họ để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở đâu."

ko.L: 그래서 달려가서 시몬 베드로와, 예수께서 사랑하시는 다른 제자에게 가서 그들에게 말한다. "[누가] 주님을 무덤에서 옮겨 갔어요. 그리고 어디에 모셔 두었는지 우리는 몰라요."
ko.B: 그래서 마리아는 시몬 베드로와, 예수께서 사랑하시는 다른 제자에게 달려가서 말했다. "누가 주님을 무덤에서 옮겨 갔어요. 어디에 모셔 두었는지 우리는 모르겠어요."
ko.R: 그래서 마리아는 시몬 베드로에게 달려갔다. 예수께서 사랑하시는 다른 제자에게도 갔다. 그리고 그들에게 말했다. "누가 주님을 무덤에서 옮겨 갔어요! 어디에 모셔 두었는지 우리는 모르겠어요."

pt.L: Ela corre, então, e vem até Simão Pedro e até o outro discípulo, a quem Jesus amava, e lhes diz: "Levaram o Senhor do túmulo, e não sabemos onde {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} puseram."
pt.B: Ela saiu correndo, então, à procura de Simão Pedro e do outro discípulo, aquele a quem Jesus amava. "Tiraram o Senhor do túmulo", disse-lhes ela, "e não sabemos onde {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} puseram."
pt.R: Então ela correu até Simão Pedro e também até o outro discípulo, aquele a quem Jesus amava. Ela disse a eles: "Alguém tirou o Senhor do túmulo! Nós não sabemos onde {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} colocaram."

am.L: ስለዚህ ትሮጣለች፤ ወደ ስምዖን ጴጥሮስና ኢየሱስ ይወደው ወደ ነበረው ወደ ሌላው ደቀ መዝሙር ትመጣለች፤ እንዲህም ትላቸዋለች፦ «ጌታን ከመቃብሩ ወስደውታል፤ የት እንዳኖሩትም አናውቅም።»
am.B: ስለዚህ ሮጣ ወደ ስምዖን ጴጥሮስና ኢየሱስ ይወደው ወደ ነበረው ወደ ሌላው ደቀ መዝሙር ሄደች። «ጌታን ከመቃብሩ አውጥተው ወስደውታል» አለቻቸው፤ «የት እንዳኖሩትም አናውቅም።»
am.R: ስለዚህ ሮጣ ወደ ስምዖን ጴጥሮስ ሄደች፤ ወደ ሌላውም ደቀ መዝሙር፣ ኢየሱስ ይወደው ወደ ነበረው ሄደች። እንዲህም አለቻቸው፦ «ጌታን ከመቃብሩ ወስደውታል! የት እንዳስቀመጡትም አናውቅም።»

decisions.choice: whom Jesus loved: the disciple of 13:23 and 19:26, here with the other verb for love
decisions.reason: Elsewhere John speaks of the disciple whom Jesus loved with the other common verb for love (13:23; 19:26; 21:7, 20); only here does he use ἐφίλει for this disciple. John uses both verbs for Jesus's love for Lazarus (11:3, 5) and for the Father's love for the Son (3:35; 5:20), so the change does not point to a different kind of love. The disciple is not named.

decisions.choice: they have taken: someone, not named
alternatives: the Jewish authorities have taken him
decisions.reason: The plural verb has no subject; it means that someone has done it. Mary does not say who. She assumes that the body has been moved, whether by grave robbers or by those in charge of the tomb, and she does not yet think of resurrection.

decisions.choice: we do not know: a hint that Mary was not alone
alternatives: we: Mary and the disciples together
we: a way of speaking, meaning only Mary
decisions.reason: Only Mary is named in verse 1, but she says "we". The other Gospels say that other women came to the tomb with her (Matthew 28:1; Mark 16:1; Luke 24:10), and the plural may reflect that. It may also be a way of speaking for the disciples as a group. In verse 13 she says "I do not know".

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus, called by the title his followers gave him
alternatives: the master (a title of respect only)
decisions.reason: Mary speaks as a disciple: she calls Jesus "the Lord" even when she thinks only of his body. The narrator uses the same title once Jesus is risen (20:20), and Mary's report in verse 18 is "I have seen the Lord".

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: Mary speaks of Jesus's body, but she means Jesus himself, so the pronoun takes the deity_pronoun setting like every pronoun for him.

decisions.choice: Someone has taken
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the subject of "they have taken" is not named (meaning decision m2); the following "they" then refers back to that someone.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to Jesus, and Spanish uses the clitic "lo", which takes the deity_pronoun setting by the book-wide rule (1:1), as do the other pronouns for Jesus in this passage (su, le, lo, me, mis, mi). "Mi" in Mary's "mi Señor" (20:13) is her own and takes none.

decisions.choice: Alguien se llevó
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable shows that the one who took him is not named (meaning decision m2). The plural "pusieron" that follows is the Spanish impersonal plural, which also names no one.

decisions.choice: On a enlevé ... où on l'a déposé (B); Quelqu'un a enlevé ... où on l'a mis (R); Ils ont enlevé (L)
alternatives: Ils ont enlevé at every level
decisions.reason: The plural verb has no subject and means that someone, not named, has done it (meaning decision m2). French says this with "on"; Literal keeps the Greek plural "ils". "L'" for Jesus takes the setting, since Mary means him, not only his body.

decisions.choice: que Jésus aimait
decisions.reason: Only here is this disciple described with the other Greek verb for love (meaning decision m1). The book-wide French choice renders both verbs "aimer", so the phrase stays the same as in 13:23 and 19:26.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on wamemweka (they have laid him)
decisions.reason: The English "him" takes the deity_pronoun setting. Swahili carries it in the object prefix -m- of the verb, which cannot take a capital, so there is nothing for the setting to change. Throughout the passage the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives (yeye, wewe, chake, zangu, yangu, wangu), so Swahili has fewer spans than English.

decisions.choice: Mary speaks of Jesus as "Chúa" and "Ngài" (with the deity_pronoun span)
decisions.reason: She is a follower, so her word for him is the respectful "Ngài", the same as the narrator's; it takes the setting as the English "him" does.

decisions.choice: Mary speaks to the disciples in the polite style (해요체: "옮겨 갔어요", "몰라요"); to the angels and the supposed gardener in 합쇼체
decisions.reason: The style guide leaves speech among equals to the scene; a woman speaking to fellow disciples, men she follows Jesus with, would naturally use 해요체, while strangers get the formal style. Jesus speaks to her in 해라체.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; "그분", "모셔" and the honorific -시- carry the respect
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change (style guide, section 7). Recorded once for this passage.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic: pronouns for Jesus (the suffixes of ወስደውታል and እንዳኖሩት) are written once
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the reader's setting for capitalised pronouns has nothing to change in Amharic. Pronouns for God and for Jesus are written plainly (the suffixes and the pronoun እርሱ) throughout this passage.

decisions.choice: ኢየሱስ ይወደው የነበረው (whom Jesus loved), the same Amharic as in 19:26
alternatives: ወዳጁ የነበረው ደቀ መዝሙር (the disciple who was his friend), to mark John's other verb for love
decisions.reason: John uses his other verb for love here of the same disciple. The book takes the two verbs as meaning the same, so Amharic keeps one phrase for the disciple throughout.

source.text: ἐξῆλθεν οὖν ὁ Πέτρος καὶ ὁ ἄλλος μαθητής, καὶ ἤρχοντο εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον.

records.literal_gloss: Went out therefore the Peter and the other disciple, and were coming to the tomb.

en.L: So Peter and the other disciple went out, and they were going to the tomb.
en.B: Peter and the other disciple then set out and made their way to the tomb.
en.R: So Peter and the other disciple left and headed for the tomb.

es.L: Salió, pues, Pedro y el otro discípulo, e iban hacia el sepulcro.
es.B: Pedro y el otro discípulo salieron enseguida y se encaminaron al sepulcro.
es.R: Pedro y el otro discípulo salieron y se fueron hacia la tumba.

fr.L: Pierre sortit donc, ainsi que l’autre disciple, et ils se rendaient au tombeau.
fr.B: Pierre et l’autre disciple partirent alors et se dirigèrent vers le tombeau.
fr.R: Alors Pierre et l’autre disciple sont partis vers le tombeau.

sw.L: Basi wakatoka Petro na yule mwanafunzi mwingine, nao walikuwa wakienda kaburini.
sw.B: Basi Petro na yule mwanafunzi mwingine waliondoka, wakashika njia kwenda kaburini.
sw.R: Basi Petro na yule mwanafunzi mwingine waliondoka, wakaelekea kaburini.

vi.L: Vậy Phi-e-rơ và môn đồ kia ra đi, và đang đi đến mộ.
vi.B: Phi-e-rơ và môn đồ kia liền lên đường đi đến mộ.
vi.R: Vậy Phi-e-rơ và môn đồ kia ra đi, hướng về phía mộ.

ko.L: 그래서 베드로와 그 다른 제자가 나가서, 무덤으로 가고 있었다.
ko.B: 베드로와 다른 제자는 곧 길을 나서서 무덤으로 향했다.
ko.R: 그래서 베드로와 다른 제자는 집을 나서 무덤으로 갔다.

pt.L: Saiu, então, Pedro e o outro discípulo, e iam ao túmulo.
pt.B: Pedro e o outro discípulo saíram, então, e foram a caminho do túmulo.
pt.R: Então Pedro e o outro discípulo saíram e foram para o túmulo.

am.L: ስለዚህ ጴጥሮስና ሌላው ደቀ መዝሙር ወጡ፤ ወደ መቃብሩም ይሄዱ ነበር።
am.B: ጴጥሮስና ሌላው ደቀ መዝሙር ተነሥተው ወደ መቃብሩ ሄዱ።
am.R: ስለዚህ ጴጥሮስና ሌላው ደቀ መዝሙር ተነሥተው ወደ መቃብሩ አመሩ።

decisions.choice: went out: a singular verb with two subjects, Peter named first
decisions.reason: The first verb is singular, as Greek often has when it comes before two subjects; Peter is named first, as the one who sets out. The second verb is plural and in the imperfect: the two were on their way to the tomb. Verse 4 then tells how they ran.

decisions.choice: were coming to the tomb: were going there
decisions.reason: The verb means to come or to go, depending on the point of view. Told from the tomb, where Mary had been, they were "coming" to it; in plain terms they were on their way there.

decisions.choice: set out and made their way (B); left and headed for (R)
decisions.reason: Natural phrases for the start of the journey and the journey under way (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Salió ... Pedro y el otro discípulo
alternatives: Salieron Pedro y el otro discípulo
decisions.reason: Spanish, like Greek, allows a singular verb before two subjects, so Literal keeps the singular and the order, with Peter named first (meaning decision m1). The imperfect "iban" keeps the journey under way (m2).

source.text: ἔτρεχον δὲ οἱ δύο ὁμοῦ· καὶ ὁ ἄλλος μαθητὴς προέδραμεν τάχιον τοῦ Πέτρου καὶ ἦλθεν πρῶτος εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον, καὶ παρακύψας βλέπει κείμενα τὰ ὀθόνια, οὐ μέντοι εἰσῆλθεν.

records.literal_gloss: Were running now the two together; and the other disciple ran ahead more quickly [than] the Peter and came first to the tomb, \v 5 and having stooped sees lying the linen cloths, not however he went in.

en.L: And the two were running together; and the other disciple ran ahead, faster than Peter, and came to the tomb first, \v 5 and stooping down he sees the linen cloths lying [there]; yet he did not go in.
en.B: The two of them ran together, but the other disciple was faster than Peter and got to the tomb ahead of him. \v 5 Bending down to look in, he saw the linen cloths lying there; he did not, however, go in.
en.R: Both of them were running, but the other disciple ran faster than Peter and got to the tomb first. \v 5 He bent down and looked inside. He saw the linen cloths lying in the tomb, but he did not go in.

es.L: Y corrían los dos juntos; y el otro discípulo corrió delante, más rápido que Pedro, y llegó primero al sepulcro, \v 5 e inclinándose ve tendidos los lienzos de lino; sin embargo, no entró.
es.B: Los dos corrían juntos, pero el otro discípulo era más rápido que Pedro y llegó al sepulcro antes que él. \v 5 Se agachó para mirar dentro y vio allí tendidos los lienzos de lino; pero no entró.
es.R: Los dos iban corriendo, pero el otro discípulo corrió más rápido que Pedro y llegó primero a la tumba. \v 5 Se agachó y miró hacia dentro. Vio los lienzos de lino que estaban en la tumba, pero no entró.

fr.L: Or les deux couraient ensemble ; et l’autre disciple courut en avant, plus vite que Pierre, et arriva le premier au tombeau, \v 5 et, s’étant penché, il voit les linges posés [là] ; pourtant il n’entra pas.
fr.B: Ils couraient tous deux ensemble, mais l’autre disciple, plus rapide que Pierre, arriva le premier au tombeau. \v 5 Il se pencha pour regarder et vit les linges posés là ; mais il n’entra pas.
fr.R: Ils couraient tous les deux, mais l’autre disciple a couru plus vite que Pierre et il est arrivé le premier au tombeau. \v 5 Il s’est penché pour regarder à l’intérieur. Il a vu les linges posés dans le tombeau, mais il n’est pas entré.

sw.L: Na wale wawili walikuwa wakikimbia pamoja; naye yule mwanafunzi mwingine akakimbia mbele, kwa kasi kuliko Petro, akafika kaburini kwanza, \v 5 na akiinama anaona vitambaa vya kitani vimelala [pale]; lakini hakuingia.
sw.B: Wote wawili walikimbia pamoja, lakini yule mwanafunzi mwingine alikuwa na kasi kuliko Petro, akafika kaburini kabla yake. \v 5 Akainama ili kutazama ndani, akaona vitambaa vya kitani vimelala pale; hata hivyo hakuingia.
sw.R: Wote wawili walikuwa wakikimbia, lakini yule mwanafunzi mwingine alikimbia kwa kasi kuliko Petro, akafika kaburini kwanza. \v 5 Aliinama, akachungulia ndani. Aliona vitambaa vya kitani vimelala kaburini, lakini hakuingia.

vi.L: Hai người cùng chạy; nhưng môn đồ kia chạy nhanh hơn Phi-e-rơ và đến mộ trước, \v 5 và cúi xuống thấy những dải vải gai nằm [đó], nhưng không vào trong.
vi.B: Hai người cùng chạy, nhưng môn đồ kia chạy nhanh hơn Phi-e-rơ và đến mộ trước. \v 5 Ông cúi xuống nhìn vào và thấy những dải vải gai nằm đó, nhưng ông không vào trong.
vi.R: Cả hai đều chạy, nhưng môn đồ kia chạy nhanh hơn Phi-e-rơ nên đến mộ trước. \v 5 Ông cúi xuống nhìn vào trong. Ông thấy những dải vải gai nằm trong mộ, nhưng ông không đi vào.

ko.L: 둘이 함께 달리고 있었는데, 다른 제자가 베드로보다 더 빨리 앞서 달려서 무덤에 먼저 왔다. \v 5 그리고 몸을 굽혀 베 천들이 놓여 있는 것을 본다. 그러나 안으로 들어가지는 않았다.
ko.B: 두 사람이 함께 달렸으나, 다른 제자가 베드로보다 빨라서 먼저 무덤에 이르렀다. \v 5 그는 몸을 굽혀 안을 들여다보고, 고운 베가 놓여 있는 것을 보았다. 그러나 안으로 들어가지는 않았다.
ko.R: 두 사람 모두 달렸지만, 다른 제자가 베드로보다 더 빨리 달려서 먼저 무덤에 닿았다. \v 5 그는 몸을 굽혀 안을 들여다보았다. 무덤 안에 고운 베 천이 놓여 있는 것이 보였다. 그러나 그는 안으로 들어가지 않았다.

pt.L: E os dois corriam juntos; e o outro discípulo correu à frente, mais depressa que Pedro, e chegou primeiro ao túmulo, \v 5 e, inclinando-se, vê as faixas de linho postas [ali]; contudo não entrou.
pt.B: Os dois corriam juntos, mas o outro discípulo era mais rápido que Pedro e chegou primeiro ao túmulo. \v 5 Inclinando-se para olhar lá dentro, viu as faixas de linho ali no chão; mas não entrou.
pt.R: Os dois estavam correndo, mas o outro discípulo correu mais depressa que Pedro e chegou primeiro ao túmulo. \v 5 Ele se abaixou e olhou lá dentro. Viu as faixas de linho no túmulo, mas não entrou.

am.L: ሁለቱም አብረው ይሮጡ ነበር፤ ሌላው ደቀ መዝሙር ግን ከጴጥሮስ ይልቅ ፈጥኖ ቀደመው፤ ወደ መቃብሩም መጀመሪያ ደረሰ፤ \v 5 ጎንበስ ብሎም የበፍታ ጨርቆቹን [በዚያ] ተቀምጠው ያያል፤ ነገር ግን አልገባም።
am.B: ሁለቱም አብረው ሮጡ፤ ሌላው ደቀ መዝሙር ግን ከጴጥሮስ ፈጥኖ ቀድሞት ወደ መቃብሩ ደረሰ። \v 5 ጎንበስ ብሎ ወደ ውስጥ ሲመለከት የበፍታ ጨርቆቹን በዚያ ተቀምጠው አየ፤ ሆኖም አልገባም።
am.R: ሁለቱም እየሮጡ ነበር፤ ሌላው ደቀ መዝሙር ግን ከጴጥሮስ ይልቅ ፈጥኖ ሮጦ መጀመሪያ ወደ መቃብሩ ደረሰ። \v 5 ጎንበስ ብሎ ወደ ውስጥ ተመለከተ። የበፍታ ጨርቆቹን በመቃብሩ ውስጥ ተቀምጠው አየ፤ ነገር ግን ወደ ውስጥ አልገባም።

decisions.choice: the linen cloths: the burial wrappings Joseph and Nicodemus had put on the body
decisions.reason: ὀθόνια is the word used in 19:40, where Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus bound Jesus's body in linen cloths with the spices. It is a different word from the strips that bound Lazarus's hands and feet (11:44). Whether these were long strips or larger pieces of linen, the word does not say.

decisions.choice: stooping down: bending to look in through a low opening
decisions.reason: The verb means to bend over in order to look into something. The openings of rock tombs were often low, so a person had to stoop to see inside. Mary does the same in verse 11.

decisions.choice: lying ... yet he did not go in: what he saw, and that he stopped there
decisions.reason: The cloths were "lying", that is, still in the tomb where the body had been. John notes that this disciple came first but did not go in, and does not say why. Verse 8 takes up the point when he does go in.

decisions.choice: Bending down to look in (B); bent down and looked inside (R)
decisions.reason: The verb itself means bending in order to look (meaning decision m2), so Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: linen cloths
decisions.reason: Every level uses the same words as in 19:40 for the same burial wrappings, and keeps them apart from the "strips of cloth" of 11:44, which is another word.

decisions.choice: lienzos de lino
decisions.reason: Every level uses the words of 19:40 for the same burial wrappings (meaning decision m1), and keeps them apart from the "vendas" of 11:44, which is another word. "Tendidos" (L, B) is "lying", still where the body had been (m3).

decisions.choice: Se agachó para mirar dentro (B); Se agachó y miró hacia dentro (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the verb itself means bending down in order to look in (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: les linges
decisions.reason: The same word as in 19:40 for the same burial wrappings (meaning decision m1), and kept apart from the "bandelettes" that bound Lazarus (11:44), which is another Greek word.

decisions.choice: vitambaa vya kitani (linen cloths)
decisions.reason: The same words as for the burial wrappings of 19:40, as meaning decision m1 says. They are kept apart from "vitambaa vya sanda", which 11:44 uses for the strips that bound Lazarus, a different Greek word. "Sanda" alone is a shroud, a single sheet, which the word does not say.

decisions.choice: as faixas de linho
decisions.reason: The same words as in 19:40 for the same burial wrappings (meaning decision m1), at every level, so the reader sees that they are the cloths Joseph and Nicodemus used.

decisions.choice: ጎንበስ ብሎ (bending down) for stooping to look in
decisions.reason: ጎንበስ አለ is the everyday way to say one bent to look through a low opening; the same verb is used of Mary in 20:11.

source.text: ἔρχεται οὖν καὶ Σίμων Πέτρος ἀκολουθῶν αὐτῷ, καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον· καὶ θεωρεῖ τὰ ὀθόνια κείμενα, καὶ τὸ σουδάριον, ὃ ἦν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ, οὐ μετὰ τῶν ὀθονίων κείμενον ἀλλὰ χωρὶς ἐντετυλιγμένον εἰς ἕνα τόπον·

records.literal_gloss: Comes therefore also Simon Peter following him, and went into the tomb; and sees the linen cloths lying, \v 7 and the face cloth, which was upon the head of him, not with the linen cloths lying but apart having been rolled up into one place;

en.L: Then Simon Peter also comes, following him, and went into the tomb; and he sees the linen cloths lying [there], \v 7 and the face cloth, which had been on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head, not lying with the linen cloths but rolled up apart in one place.
en.B: Then Simon Peter, who had been following him, came and went into the tomb. He saw the linen cloths lying there, \v 7 and the face cloth that had been on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head. It was not lying with the linen cloths; it was rolled up in a place of its own, apart from them.
en.R: Simon Peter came up behind him and went right into the tomb. He saw the linen cloths lying there. \v 7 He also saw the cloth that had been around Jesus's head. It was not with the linen cloths. It was rolled up and lying by itself.

es.L: Llega, pues, también Simón Pedro, que lo seguía, y entró en el sepulcro; y ve tendidos los lienzos de lino, \v 7 y el sudario, que había estado sobre {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cabeza, no tendido con los lienzos, sino enrollado aparte en un lugar.
es.B: Luego llegó Simón Pedro, que venía detrás de él, y entró en el sepulcro. Vio allí tendidos los lienzos de lino, \v 7 y también el paño que había estado sobre {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cabeza. Este no estaba con los lienzos, sino enrollado en un lugar aparte.
es.R: Simón Pedro llegó detrás de él y entró directamente en la tumba. Vio allí los lienzos de lino. \v 7 También vio el paño que había cubierto la cabeza de Jesús. No estaba con los lienzos de lino. Estaba enrollado y puesto aparte.

fr.L: Simon Pierre, qui le suivait, arrive donc aussi, et il entra dans le tombeau ; et il regarde les linges posés [là], \v 7 et le suaire, qui avait été sur {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} tête, non pas posé avec les linges, mais roulé à part, en un endroit distinct.
fr.B: Simon Pierre, qui le suivait, arriva à son tour et entra dans le tombeau. Il vit les linges posés là, \v 7 et le suaire qui avait été sur {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} tête. Celui-ci n’était pas posé avec les linges ; il était roulé et mis à part, à un autre endroit.
fr.R: Simon Pierre est arrivé derrière lui, et il est entré directement dans le tombeau. Il a vu les linges posés là. \v 7 Il a vu aussi le tissu qui avait entouré la tête de Jésus. Ce tissu n’était pas avec les linges. Il était roulé et posé à part.

sw.L: Basi anakuja pia Simoni Petro, akimfuata, akaingia kaburini; naye anatazama vitambaa vya kitani vimelala [pale], \v 7 na kitambaa cha uso, kilichokuwa juu ya kichwa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}, si kimelala pamoja na vitambaa vya kitani, bali kimekunjwa kando mahali pa pekee.
sw.B: Kisha Simoni Petro, aliyekuwa akimfuata, alifika, akaingia kaburini. Akaona vitambaa vya kitani vimelala pale, \v 7 na kile kitambaa cha uso kilichokuwa juu ya kichwa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}. Kitambaa hicho hakikuwa pamoja na vitambaa vya kitani; kilikuwa kimekunjwa na kuwekwa kando peke yake.
sw.R: Simoni Petro alifika nyuma yake, akaingia moja kwa moja ndani ya kaburi. Aliona vitambaa vya kitani vimelala pale. \v 7 Aliona pia kitambaa kilichokuwa kimezungushwa kichwani pa Yesu. Hakikuwa pamoja na vitambaa vya kitani. Kilikuwa kimekunjwa, na kimewekwa peke yake.

vi.L: Rồi Si-môn Phi-e-rơ, theo sau ông, cũng đến, và đã vào trong mộ; ông thấy những dải vải gai nằm [đó], \v 7 và cái khăn đã ở trên đầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, không nằm chung với những dải vải gai nhưng được cuốn lại để riêng một chỗ.
vi.B: Rồi Si-môn Phi-e-rơ, người theo sau, cũng đến và đi vào trong mộ. Ông thấy những dải vải gai nằm đó, \v 7 và cái khăn đã che đầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Khăn ấy không nằm chung với những dải vải gai mà được cuốn lại, để riêng ở một chỗ.
vi.R: Si-môn Phi-e-rơ theo sau ông, đến nơi và đi thẳng vào trong mộ. Ông thấy những dải vải gai nằm đó. \v 7 Ông cũng thấy cái khăn đã quấn quanh đầu Đức Giê-xu. Khăn ấy không nằm chung với những dải vải gai, nhưng được cuốn lại và để riêng một chỗ.

ko.L: 그러자 시몬 베드로도 그를 따라 와서 무덤 안으로 들어갔다. 그리고 베 천들이 놓여 있는 것을 본다. \v 7 또 그분의 머리에 있던 수건은 베 천들과 함께 놓여 있지 않고, 따로 한곳에 말려 있었다.
ko.B: 뒤따라오던 시몬 베드로가 도착하여 무덤 안으로 들어갔다. 그는 고운 베가 놓여 있는 것을 보았고, \v 7 예수의 머리를 감쌌던 수건도 보았다. 그 수건은 고운 베와 함께 놓여 있지 않고, 따로 한곳에 말려 있었다.
ko.R: 시몬 베드로가 뒤따라와서 곧장 무덤 안으로 들어갔다. 그도 고운 베 천이 놓여 있는 것을 보았다. \v 7 예수의 머리를 감쌌던 수건도 보았다. 그 수건은 고운 베 천과 함께 있지 않았다. 따로 말린 채 한쪽에 놓여 있었다.

pt.L: Vem, então, também Simão Pedro, seguindo-o, e entrou no túmulo; e vê as faixas de linho postas [ali], \v 7 e o pano que estivera sobre a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} cabeça, não posto com as faixas de linho, mas enrolado à parte, num lugar.
pt.B: Depois chegou Simão Pedro, que vinha atrás dele, e entrou no túmulo. Ele viu as faixas de linho ali no chão, \v 7 e também o pano que estivera sobre a cabeça de Jesus. Esse pano não estava com as faixas de linho; estava enrolado num lugar à parte, separado delas.
pt.R: Simão Pedro chegou logo depois e entrou direto no túmulo. Ele viu as faixas de linho ali no chão. \v 7 Viu também o pano que tinha estado em volta da cabeça de Jesus. Esse pano não estava junto com as faixas de linho. Estava enrolado e separado, num lugar só para ele.

am.L: ስምዖን ጴጥሮስም ደግሞ እየተከተለው ይመጣል፤ ወደ መቃብሩም ገባ፤ የበፍታ ጨርቆቹንም ተቀምጠው ያያል፤ \v 7 በራሱም ላይ የነበረውን የራስ ጨርቅ ከበፍታ ጨርቆቹ ጋር ተቀምጦ ሳይሆን ለብቻው በአንድ ስፍራ ተጠቅልሎ [ያያል]።
am.B: ከዚያም እየተከተለው የነበረው ስምዖን ጴጥሮስ መጥቶ ወደ መቃብሩ ገባ። የበፍታ ጨርቆቹን በዚያ ተቀምጠው አየ፤ \v 7 በራሱ ላይ የነበረውንም የራስ ጨርቅ አየ። ይህ ጨርቅ ከበፍታ ጨርቆቹ ጋር አልተቀመጠም ነበር፤ ከእነርሱ ተለይቶ ለብቻው በአንድ ስፍራ ተጠቅልሎ ነበር።
am.R: ስምዖን ጴጥሮስ ከኋላው ደረሰ፤ በቀጥታም ወደ መቃብሩ ውስጥ ገባ። የበፍታ ጨርቆቹን በዚያ ተቀምጠው አየ። \v 7 በኢየሱስ ራስ ዙሪያ የነበረውንም ጨርቅ አየ። ይህ ጨርቅ ከበፍታ ጨርቆቹ ጋር አልነበረም፤ ተጠቅልሎ ለብቻው ተቀምጦ ነበር።

decisions.choice: the face cloth: a smaller cloth for the head and face
decisions.reason: σουδάριον is the cloth that was tied around Lazarus's face (11:44). Here it had been on Jesus's head. Lazarus came out of his tomb still bound in his wrappings and had to be set free; Jesus has left his behind.

decisions.choice: rolled up apart in one place: folded or rolled together, lying by itself
alternatives: still in the shape in which it had wrapped the head
decisions.reason: ἐντετυλιγμένον means wrapped, rolled or folded up. The form is passive and perfect: the cloth lay rolled up. John does not say who rolled it. "Into one place" means in a place on its own, apart from the linen cloths.

decisions.choice: the order of the grave clothes: a detail that tells against a hurried theft
alternatives: a detail with no further point
decisions.reason: John describes the cloths with care, but he does not explain them. Their state does not fit Mary's fear that the body had been carried off (verse 2): those who move or steal a body do not first unwrap it and leave the cloths behind in order. The detail prepares for what the other disciple sees and believes in verse 8.

decisions.choice: comes ... went in: Peter arrives second but goes in first
decisions.reason: John moves between the present ("comes", "sees") and the past ("went in"); see the historic present at 20:1. Peter follows the other disciple, but he goes straight into the tomb.

decisions.choice: Jesus's head
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus, since "his head" straight after "him" (the other disciple) could be misread.

decisions.choice: face cloth (L, B); the cloth that had been around Jesus's head (R)
decisions.reason: "Face cloth" names the same cloth as at Lazarus's tomb (11:44, "a cloth tied around his face"); Readable describes it by where it had been.

decisions.choice: sudario (L); paño (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same words as at Lazarus's tomb (11:44, where Literal has "sudario" and Balanced and Readable "paño"), so readers can link the two cloths (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: la cabeza de Jesús
decisions.reason: As in English: "su cabeza" straight after "él" (the other disciple) could be misread.

decisions.choice: le suaire (L, B); le tissu qui avait entouré la tête de Jésus (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the cloth that had been around Lazarus's face, rendered "un linge" at 11:44 (meaning decision m1). Here "linges" already names the other burial cloths, so Literal and Balanced use "suaire", the old French word from the same Latin source as the Greek; today it can call to mind a whole shroud, so Readable describes the cloth by where it had been.

decisions.choice: kitambaa cha uso (face cloth) (L, B); the cloth that had been wrapped around Jesus's head (R)
decisions.reason: The same cloth as the one tied over Lazarus's face in 11:44, where Swahili also says "kitambaa", so the link between the two tombs stays visible (meaning decision m1). "Leso" today means a handkerchief or a woman's printed cloth, which would mislead.

decisions.choice: "수건" for the face cloth at every level; "베 천들" (L), "고운 베" (B), "고운 베 천" (R) for the linen cloths, as in 19:40
decisions.reason: The same Korean words as at the burial (19:40), so the reader sees that the cloths Joseph and Nicodemus wrapped are the ones left behind.

decisions.choice: o pano que estivera sobre a sua cabeça (L); o pano que estivera sobre a cabeça de Jesus (B); o pano que tinha estado em volta da cabeça de Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: The same word as at Lazarus's tomb (11:44), where Portuguese says "um pano" (meaning decision m1), so every level says "o pano" and tells where it had been, which keeps the link the English keeps with "face cloth". "Sudário" is the traditional word but would hide that link; "lenço" suggests a handkerchief.

decisions.choice: a cabeça de Jesus
decisions.reason: After "que vinha atrás dele" (the other disciple), Portuguese "sua cabeça" could be read as that disciple's head, so Balanced names Jesus, as the English Readable does; Literal keeps the possessive.

decisions.choice: የራስ ጨርቅ (L, B), በኢየሱስ ራስ ዙሪያ የነበረው ጨርቅ (R) for the face cloth
decisions.reason: The cloth was for the head and face of the dead; ሻሽ and መሐረብ name everyday items of the living.

source.text: τότε οὖν εἰσῆλθεν καὶ ὁ ἄλλος μαθητὴς ὁ ἐλθὼν πρῶτος εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον, καὶ εἶδεν καὶ ἐπίστευσεν·

records.literal_gloss: Then therefore went in also the other disciple, the [one] having come first to the tomb, and he saw and believed;

vi.L: Bấy giờ môn đồ kia, là người đã đến mộ trước, cũng vào trong, và ông đã thấy và tin.
vi.B: Bấy giờ môn đồ kia, người đã đến mộ trước, cũng vào trong; ông thấy và tin.
vi.R: Rồi môn đồ kia, là người đã đến mộ trước, cũng vào trong. Ông thấy, và ông tin.

ko.L: 그때 무덤에 먼저 왔던 다른 제자도 들어갔다. 그리고 보고 믿었다.
ko.B: 그제야 먼저 무덤에 왔던 다른 제자도 들어가서, 보고 믿었다.
ko.R: 그때 무덤에 먼저 도착했던 다른 제자도 들어갔다. 그는 보고 믿었다.

pt.L: Então entrou também o outro discípulo, o que tinha chegado primeiro ao túmulo, e viu e creu.
pt.B: Então o outro discípulo, que tinha chegado primeiro ao túmulo, também entrou; e ele viu e creu.
pt.R: Então o outro discípulo também entrou, aquele que tinha chegado primeiro ao túmulo. Ele viu e acreditou.

am.L: በዚያን ጊዜም አስቀድሞ ወደ መቃብሩ የመጣው ሌላው ደቀ መዝሙር ደግሞ ገባ፤ አየ፤ አመነም።
am.B: ከዚያም አስቀድሞ ወደ መቃብሩ የደረሰው ሌላው ደቀ መዝሙር ደግሞ ገባ፤ አይቶም አመነ።
am.R: ከዚያም ሌላው ደቀ መዝሙር ደግሞ ገባ፤ እርሱ መጀመሪያ ወደ መቃብሩ የደረሰው ነበር። አየ፤ አመነም።

decisions.choice: believed: he came to believe that Jesus had risen
alternatives: he believed Mary's report that the body had been taken
decisions.reason: John does not say what he believed. The most natural sense is that what he saw in the tomb brought him to believe that Jesus had been raised. Verse 9 explains why it took seeing: they did not yet understand from the Scriptures that he must rise. Some take the verb to mean only that he now believed Mary's report that the body was gone, but John uses the verb for full belief, and he would hardly say "he saw and believed" of that alone. This disciple believes without yet seeing Jesus himself; compare 20:29.

decisions.choice: saw: he saw the empty tomb and the cloths
alternatives: a growing depth of sight from one verb to the next
decisions.reason: John uses three verbs for seeing in these verses: βλέπει (verse 5), θεωρεῖ (verse 6) and εἶδεν (here). In John these verbs overlap a great deal, and the change need not mark steps of deeper insight. What matters is that this time seeing leads to believing.

decisions.choice: the one who had come first: he reached the tomb first but went in second
decisions.reason: John repeats that this disciple arrived first (verse 4). The order is told plainly; the text draws no contest between the two disciples from it.

decisions.choice: he saw and believed
alternatives: he saw and believed that Jesus had risen
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the two verbs without an object, as John does, so that what he believed stays as open as in the original (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: vio y creyó, with no object
decisions.reason: As in English: every level keeps the two verbs without saying what he believed, as John does (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: አመነ (believed) at every level
decisions.reason: Believe is a key term in John and keeps its one Amharic verb, ማመን, at every level, here as everywhere in the book.

source.text: οὐδέπω γὰρ ᾔδεισαν τὴν γραφὴν ὅτι δεῖ αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῆναι.

records.literal_gloss: Not yet for they knew the scripture, that it is necessary him from [the] dead to rise.

en.L: For they did not yet know the Scripture, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} must rise from [the] dead.
en.B: For as yet they did not understand the Scripture, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} must rise from the dead.
en.R: Until then they had not understood that the Scriptures said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had to rise from the dead.

es.L: Porque todavía no conocían la Escritura: que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} tenía que resucitar de [los] muertos.
es.B: Pues todavía no habían comprendido la Escritura, según la cual {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} tenía que resucitar de entre los muertos.
es.R: Hasta ese momento no habían entendido que las Escrituras decían que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} tenía que resucitar de entre los muertos.

fr.L: Car ils ne connaissaient pas encore l’Écriture, [qui dit] qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} devait ressusciter d’entre les morts.

fr.R: Jusque-là, ils n’avaient pas compris que les Écritures annonçaient qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} devait ressusciter.

vi.L: Vì họ chưa biết Kinh Thánh, rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phải sống lại từ [cõi] chết.
vi.B: Vì đến lúc ấy họ vẫn chưa hiểu lời Kinh Thánh nói rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phải sống lại từ cõi chết.

ko.L: 그들은 그분이 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살아나셔야 한다는 성경 [말씀]을 아직 알지 못했기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그들은 그분이 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살아나셔야 한다는 성경 말씀을 아직 깨닫지 못하고 있었다.
ko.R: 그때까지 그들은 예수께서 죽은 사람들 가운데서 다시 살아나셔야 한다는 성경 말씀을 깨닫지 못했다.

pt.L: Pois ainda não conheciam a Escritura, que era necessário que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} ressuscitasse dos mortos.
pt.B: Pois até então não tinham entendido a Escritura, segundo a qual {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} devia ressuscitar dos mortos.
pt.R: Até aquele momento eles não tinham entendido que as Escrituras diziam que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tinha de ressuscitar dos mortos.

am.L: ከሙታን ሊነሣ እንደሚገባው መጽሐፍን ገና አላወቁም ነበርና።
am.B: ከሙታን ሊነሣ እንደሚገባው የሚናገረውን የመጽሐፍ ቃል ገና አላስተዋሉም ነበርና።
am.R: እስከዚያ ጊዜ ድረስ ኢየሱስ ከሞት መነሣት እንዳለበት መጻሕፍት እንደሚናገሩ አላስተዋሉም ነበር።

decisions.choice: knew: understood
decisions.reason: They knew the Scriptures as words; what they did not yet know was their meaning. John says the same of the disciples' understanding after the resurrection at 2:22 and 12:16. The "they" are the two disciples, and the verse explains why it was seeing, not the Scriptures, that brought the other disciple to believe.

decisions.choice: the Scripture: John names no passage
decisions.reason: The singular may point to one passage or speak of Scripture as a whole. The first Christians found the resurrection foretold in Psalm 16:10 (Acts 2:24-32; 13:35) and spoke of Christ being raised "according to the Scriptures" (1 Corinthians 15:4; Luke 24:25-27, 44-46). John does not say which text he has in mind.

decisions.choice: must: the necessity of God's plan
decisions.reason: δεῖ is the word John uses for what has to happen by God's will: the Son of Man "must" be lifted up (3:14; 12:34). The rising from the dead was part of that plan, not an accident.

decisions.choice: understand (B); had not understood (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "understand" for the sense of the verb here (meaning decision m1); Literal keeps "know".

decisions.choice: the Scriptures said
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plural, the common way of speaking of the whole of Scripture, since John names no one passage (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: comprendido (B); entendido, las Escrituras (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: they knew the words but not their meaning (meaning decision m1), as at 12:16 ("no entendieron"). Readable uses the plural for Scripture as a whole, since John names no passage (m2). "Tenía que" carries the necessity of God's plan (m3).

decisions.choice: l'Écriture, [qui dit] qu'il devait ... (L); d'entre les morts without brackets
decisions.reason: French cannot join "l'Écriture" directly to a clause beginning "que", so Literal brackets the words that link them. The article in "d'entre les morts" is part of the fixed French phrase and needs no bracket. Balanced and Readable say "compris" for the sense of the verb (meaning decision m1).

source.text: ἀπῆλθον οὖν πάλιν πρὸς αὑτοὺς οἱ μαθηταί.

es.R: Después, los dos discípulos regresaron a donde se estaban quedando.

decisions.choice: to themselves: to their own lodgings
decisions.reason: The phrase means to their own place, home. They were in Jerusalem for the Passover, so it means where they were staying in or near the city, not their homes in Galilee. Luke uses a similar phrase of Peter going home from the tomb (Luke 24:12).

decisions.choice: the disciples: the two who had gone to the tomb
decisions.reason: The article points back to Peter and the other disciple of verses 3-8.

decisions.choice: to where they were staying (B, R); the two disciples (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "to themselves" means here (meaning decision m1); Readable also says which disciples are meant (m2).

decisions.choice: donde se alojaban (B); a donde se estaban quedando, los dos discípulos (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: their lodgings in Jerusalem, not their homes (meaning decision m1); Readable says which disciples (m2).

decisions.choice: chez eux (L); là où ils logeaient (B, R)
decisions.reason: French "chez eux" renders the Greek "to themselves" without a supplied word, but it suggests their homes in Galilee; they were staying in or near Jerusalem for the Passover (meaning decision m1), so Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: kwenda kwao (to their own place)
decisions.reason: Swahili "kwao" means to one's own home or place, the same idiom as the Greek "to themselves" (meaning decision m1), so Literal needs no bracket where the English supplies "[places]". Balanced and Readable say that it was where they were staying in Jerusalem, as the English does.

decisions.choice: but Mary was standing: the scene turns from the two disciples to her
decisions.reason: The verb has the form of a past perfect, but with this verb it describes a lasting state: she was standing there. John does not say that she came back with the two disciples or when she arrived; he simply shows her at the tomb after they have gone.

decisions.choice: weeping: crying aloud in grief

decisions.choice: two angels: messengers from God
decisions.reason: The word can mean any messenger, but here they are heavenly beings. White clothing marks such beings in the Gospels and Acts (Matthew 28:3; Mark 16:5; Acts 1:10). The two disciples saw no angels; Mary does.

decisions.choice: in white: in white clothes
decisions.reason: The adjective is plural with no noun; "clothes" is understood, a common way of speaking (Revelation 3:4-5).

decisions.choice: one at the head and one at the feet: where the body had been, with no further sign drawn
alternatives: an echo of the two cherubim over the ark
decisions.reason: Some readers have seen in the two angels a picture of the two cherubim at either end of the cover of the ark (Exodus 25:18-22). John draws no such link; the detail places the angels exactly where the body had lain.

decisions.choice: [to look] (L); stooped to look (B); bent down and looked (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to bend in order to look (see verse 5). Literal shows the supplied words in brackets.

decisions.choice: in white clothes (B); dressed in white (R)
decisions.reason: Supplies the understood "clothes" (meaning decision m2); "in white" alone is the Literal form.

decisions.choice: [para mirar] (L); para mirar (B); se agachó y miró (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 5: the verb means bending in order to look. Literal brackets the supplied words.

decisions.choice: de blanco (L); vestidos de blanco (B, R)
decisions.reason: Spanish "de blanco" already means "dressed in white", so Literal needs no bracketed word for the understood clothes (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: wamevaa [nguo] nyeupe (L); waliovaa nguo nyeupe (B, R)
decisions.reason: Swahili cannot say "in white" with the noun left out, as Greek and English can (meaning decision m2): the colour word must agree with a noun, and "in" becomes a verb of wearing. The verb is part of saying "in", so Literal brackets only the supplied "nguo".

decisions.choice: Woman: a respectful address
decisions.reason: See the note at 2:4. The address was courteous; Jesus uses it to his mother (2:4; 19:26), to the Samaritan woman (4:21), and to Mary in verse 15.

decisions.choice: why are you weeping?: a question that hints there is no cause for grief
decisions.reason: The angels do not ask for information. Their question gently suggests that weeping is out of place, since the one she mourns is not dead. Jesus asks the same question in verse 15.

decisions.choice: Woman
decisions.reason: As at 2:4 and 4:21: "Woman" on its own can sound cold, but keeping it lets readers connect the passages; the footnote says it was respectful.

decisions.choice: Dear woman
decisions.reason: For young readers "Woman" sounds rude, which the Greek is not; "Dear woman" keeps the courtesy (meaning decision m1), as at 4:21.

decisions.choice: Mujer (L, B); Señora (R)
decisions.reason: As at 2:4: the Greek address is respectful (meaning decision m1). Literal and Balanced keep "Mujer" so readers can link the passages; the footnote says it was courteous. Readable, like the English "Dear woman", uses "Señora", the courteous Spanish address. At 4:21 Spanish Readable kept "mujer"; a reviewer should settle one Readable form for 4:21 and 20:13-15.

decisions.choice: Femme (L, B); Madame (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "Femme", so that readers can connect the passages (2:4; 19:26); the address was respectful (meaning decision m1). For young readers "Femme" sounds cold, and "Chère femme" is not French usage; Readable says "Madame", the courteous address, which pairs with Mary's "Monsieur" in verse 15. As there, the speakers still say "tu". A native reviewer may prefer to drop the address, as Readable does at 4:21.

decisions.choice: Mama at every level
decisions.reason: As at 2:4 and 4:21: the Greek address is respectful (meaning decision m1), and "Mwanamke!" said to a woman's face is rude in Swahili. "Mama" is the respectful address to any grown woman, so it keeps the tone at every level. The same in verse 15.

decisions.choice: "Hỡi bà" (L, B); "Bà ơi" (R); Mary is "bà" throughout
decisions.reason: The Greek "Woman" is respectful. "Hỡi bà" is a dignified vocative; "Này bà" would sound curt and "Hỡi người đàn bà" cold. Readable uses the everyday warm "Bà ơi", as the English has "Dear woman". The same in 20:15.

decisions.choice: "여자여" (L); "여인이여" (B, R), here and in 20:15
decisions.reason: The Greek address is respectful (meaning decision); the style guide keeps "여자여" at Literal and gives "여인이여" at Balanced and Readable, which sounds courteous rather than cold. The English Readable says "Dear woman".

decisions.choice: Senhora
decisions.reason: Where the English Readable says "Dear woman" for the courteous address (meaning decision m1), Portuguese "Mulher" on its own sounds blunt and "Querida" too intimate; "Senhora" is the polite Brazilian way to address a woman one does not know. Literal and Balanced keep "Mulher", as the English keeps "Woman", so readers can link 2:4 and 19:26.

decisions.choice: ሴት ሆይ (L, B); እኅቴ (R)
alternatives: እናቴ (mother), used as a polite address to an older woman
decisions.reason: The address is respectful. ሴት ሆይ keeps John's word with a formal vocative that is not cold; Readable uses እኅቴ (my sister), the warm, polite way to speak to a woman in Amharic, for the English "Dear woman". The same in 20:15.

decisions.choice: my Lord: Jesus, the master she followed

decisions.choice: I do not know: now singular
decisions.reason: She repeats what she said to the disciples (verse 2), but now speaks only for herself.

decisions.choice: a word that opens direct speech
decisions.reason: ὅτι here introduces her words as a quotation; it does not mean "that" or "because".

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: She speaks of Jesus, so the pronoun takes the deity_pronoun setting, as in verse 2.

decisions.choice: Someone has taken

decisions.choice: My Lord has been taken away

decisions.choice: Alguien se llevó
decisions.reason: As in verse 2: Readable shows that the subject is not named.

decisions.choice: A mi Señor se lo han llevado
alternatives: Se han llevado a mi Señor
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced puts "mi Señor" first, where her grief is; the impersonal plural names no one (meaning decision m2 at verse 2).

decisions.choice: Levaram embora o meu Senhor

decisions.reason: Portuguese says that the takers are not named with the third person plural and no subject, which is more natural than the passive the English Balanced uses; "o meu Senhor" still ends the clause, where the stress falls.

decisions.choice: turned to the things behind: turned around
decisions.reason: The phrase means to turn and look back. She turns away from the tomb and the angels.

decisions.choice: she did not know that it was Jesus: she did not recognize him
decisions.reason: John does not say why. Others too fail at first to recognize the risen Jesus (Luke 24:16; John 21:4). It may have been her tears and the early light, or something changed in him; the text leaves it open. She knows him when he calls her by name (verse 16).

decisions.choice: that it was Jesus: a present tense inside reported thought
decisions.reason: Greek keeps the tense of the original thought ("it is Jesus"), where the story's past would be expected.

decisions.choice: did not realize
decisions.reason: The plain word for not recognizing someone; "know" in Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: no se dio cuenta
decisions.reason: As in English: the plain way to say she did not recognize him (meaning decision m2); Literal and Balanced keep "no sabía".

decisions.choice: whom are you seeking?: an echo of Jesus's first words in this Gospel
alternatives: an ordinary question with no echo
decisions.reason: Jesus's first words in John are "What are you seeking?" (1:38), and he asks "Whom are you seeking?" of those who come to arrest him (18:4, 7). John may mean the reader to hear these together. The link is not certain; the question also makes plain sense on its own.

decisions.choice: whom: a person, not a thing
decisions.reason: Mary is looking for a body. Jesus asks whom she is looking for: the one she seeks is a living person.

decisions.choice: seeking (L); looking for (B, R)
decisions.reason: Everyday English at Balanced and Readable; Literal keeps "seeking", as at 1:38 and 18:4, so that the link can be seen (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: buscas at every level
decisions.reason: Spanish "buscar" is the everyday verb for both "seek" and "look for", so every level can keep the wording of 1:38 and 18:4 ("¿Qué buscan?", "¿A quién buscan?") and the possible echo (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Qui cherches-tu ? (every level)
decisions.reason: French "chercher" is both "seek" and "look for", so every level can keep the everyday verb and the link with 1:38 ("Que cherchez-vous ?") and 18:4, 7 stays visible (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: kutafuta (seek, look for) at every level
decisions.reason: Swahili "kutafuta" is both the plain word and the one used for Jesus's first question in 1:38 ("Mnatafuta nini?"), so every level keeps the possible echo (meaning decision m1) without the change of word the English makes between Literal and Balanced.

records.literal_gloss: She, thinking that the gardener he is, says to him, "Sir, if you carried him, tell me where you laid him, and I him will take."

en.L: Thinking that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was the gardener, she says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Sir, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have carried {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} off, tell me where {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have laid {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and I will take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away."
en.B: Supposing {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was the gardener, she said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Sir, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the one who has carried {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} off, tell me where {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and I will take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away."
en.R: She thought {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was the gardener. So she said, "Sir, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have taken {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away, tell me where {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then I will go and get {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

fr.L: Celle-ci, pensant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était le jardinier, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Monsieur, si c’est {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}as emporté, dis-moi où {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}as déposé, et moi, je {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}enlèverai. »

fr.R: Elle a cru qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était le jardinier. Alors elle a dit : « Monsieur, si c’est {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}as emporté, dis-moi où {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}as mis. Et j’irai {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} chercher. »

alignments.target_span: are the one who has carried

decisions.choice: Sir: a polite address to a man she does not recognize
decisions.reason: Κύριε is the word that means Lord, but it was also the ordinary courteous way to address a man (see 4:11). Mary thinks she is speaking to the gardener, so she uses it as a polite address. A moment before she spoke of "my Lord" (verse 13).

decisions.choice: the gardener: the man who looked after the garden where the tomb was
decisions.reason: The tomb was in a garden near the place of crucifixion (19:41). Someone looking after the garden early in the morning might well have moved a body, so her guess is a natural one.

decisions.choice: if you have carried him off ... I will take him: both pronouns stressed
decisions.reason: The pronoun "you" is written out, which stresses it: she suspects this man. "I" is also stressed: she herself will take the body away. She does not stop to think how one woman could carry it.

decisions.choice: carried off: lifted and carried away
decisions.reason: ἐβάστασας means to pick up and carry. With "take" at the end of the sentence, it pictures the body being moved from place to place.

decisions.choice: Sir
decisions.reason: Mary does not know who he is, so every level has "Sir" (meaning decision m1); "Lord" would put in her mouth a recognition she has not yet made. The footnote gives "Lord", the other sense of the same Greek word.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}; {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}
decisions.reason: Mary does not recognize Jesus, but every pronoun here refers to him: the man she speaks to and the body she speaks of. All of them take the deity_pronoun setting, as when the Samaritan woman speaks to him (4:11).

decisions.choice: Señor, opening her words (L); señor, lowercase after the condition (B, R)
alternatives: Señor, opening her words at every level
decisions.reason: Spanish "señor" is both the polite "sir" and "Lord" (4:11). Mary does not know who he is (meaning decision m1), so it is the polite address. Literal keeps the Greek order, where the word takes a capital only because it begins her speech; Balanced and Readable put it after the condition, where the lowercase shows that she says "sir". The footnote gives "Lord".

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}
decisions.reason: The Greek writes the pronoun out, and Spanish keeps the stressed "tú" (meaning decision m3). It refers to Jesus, so it takes the setting, as when the Samaritan woman speaks to him (4:9); "le" and "lo" for him take it too, by the book-wide rule (1:1); "te" in "te lo llevaste" is reflexive and is written plain.

decisions.choice: el hortelano
decisions.reason: The tomb was in a garden, which John 18-19 Spanish calls "huerto" (18:1, 19:41), so the man who looks after it is "el hortelano" (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Monsieur
decisions.reason: Mary does not know who he is, so every level has "Monsieur", the French courtesy address (meaning decision m1), as in 4:11 and 4:49; "Seigneur" would put in her mouth a recognition she has not yet made. With "Monsieur" she still says "tu", as the French brief has everyone do to one person.

decisions.choice: c'est {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui {{deity_pronoun:l'|L'}}as emporté; où {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:l'|L'}}as déposé
decisions.reason: Every pronoun here is for Jesus, the man she speaks to and the body she speaks of, so all take the setting, as in the English. The stressed "you" (meaning decision m3) is shown by "c'est toi qui", and the stressed "I" at Literal by "moi, je".

decisions.choice: bwana, lowercase, after the first clause
decisions.reason: Swahili has one word for "Sir" and "Lord". Mary does not know who he is, so it is the polite "bwana" (meaning decision m1), as with the Samaritan woman in 4:11. At the start of the sentence it would need a capital and read as "Lord", so it stands after the first clause, as in 4:11. The pronouns for Jesus ("yeye", "wewe") take the deity_pronoun setting, as in English; Mary's own "nami mwenyewe" (I myself, the stressed pronoun of meaning decision m3) does not.

decisions.choice: "Thưa ông" for "Sir", "ông" for "you", with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As the style guide: someone who does not recognise Jesus says "thưa ông". Mary thinks she is speaking to the gardener, so "ông" is her word for a stranger and is not capitalised where the English "You" has a span. The absent body she speaks of is still "Ngài" to her, with the span.

decisions.choice: "선생님" for kyrie, and "[선생님께서]" (L) / "선생님께서" (B, R) for the stressed "you"
decisions.reason: Mary takes him for the gardener, so she uses the polite address for a man she does not know (style guide, section 6); "당신" would sound rude, and "주님" would anticipate her recognition in 20:16. The repeated title keeps the stress on "you".

decisions.choice: Senhor, se o senhor ... diga-me
decisions.reason: Mary takes him for the gardener (meaning decision m1), so she speaks as a woman to a man she does not know, with "o senhor" and the third-person imperative "diga"; "tu" would show a recognition she has not yet made. "O senhor" is her polite address, not a title of Jesus, so it takes no deity_pronoun setting; the pronouns for the body she is looking for do.

decisions.choice: ጌታዬ (Sir), with the plain አንተ forms
alternatives: ጌታ ሆይ (Lord), the disciples' address to Jesus
decisions.reason: Mary takes him for the gardener, so she says ጌታዬ, the polite address to a man, while ጌታ ሆይ stays for those who address Jesus as Lord. She uses አንተ, the Bible's familiar address, which the book keeps for everyone who speaks to Jesus.

decisions.choice: Rabbouni: "my teacher", a warm form of Rabbi, which John translates

decisions.choice: in Hebrew: in the language of the Jews of the land
decisions.reason: As at 5:2 and 19:13, 17, 20, John means the local language, which in daily speech was mostly Aramaic. The form of Rabbouni is Aramaic.

decisions.choice: turning: she turns to face him fully
alternatives: she turns away from the tomb a second time
decisions.reason: She had already turned around in verse 14. John does not explain the second turning. It may be that she had turned back toward the tomb while she spoke, or that she now turns fully to him once she knows his voice.

decisions.choice: Rabbouni! (which means Teacher)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the word Mary said and John's own translation, as at 1:38 with Rabbi.

decisions.choice: turned toward him
decisions.reason: Readable shows that she turns to face Jesus (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: ¡Rabuni! with John's translation, Maestro
decisions.reason: As at 1:38 with "Rabí": every level keeps the word Mary said, spelled as Spanish reads it, and John's own translation, "Maestro" as at 1:38. "En hebreo" as at 5:2 (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: se volvió hacia {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable shows that she turns to face Jesus (meaning decision m3); the stressed pronoun takes the setting.

decisions.choice: Maître
decisions.reason: As at 1:38, where John translates Rabbi with the same word: "Maître" is how French addresses a teacher with respect. Every level keeps "Rabbouni" and John's translation (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Rabuni (maana yake ni Mwalimu)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the word Mary said, in Swahili spelling, with John's own translation, as 1:38 does with "Rabi" ("maana yake ni Mwalimu"). Keeping "Rabuni" apart from "Rabi" shows that she uses the fuller, warmer form (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "Ra-bu-ni"; "Thầy"
decisions.reason: The name is spelled in the Protestant style of "Ra-bi". John's own translation is given with "Thầy", the word the disciples use for Jesus throughout.

decisions.choice: "랍오니", explained as "선생님"
decisions.reason: The established Protestant spelling of the word; John translates it himself, so Korean keeps the word and his explanation.

decisions.choice: Raboni! (que quer dizer Mestre)
decisions.reason: The Aramaic word is spelled as Portuguese writes its sounds (style §11), not in the English transliteration. "Mestre" is the Portuguese word for a teacher of disciples; "professor" would sound like a school.

decisions.choice: «ረቡኒ!» and (ትርጉሙም መምህር ማለት ነው)

Ve más bien a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} {{gender:hermanos y hermanas|hermanos}} con este mensaje: “Subo a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre y {{plural_you:Padre de ustedes|vuestro Padre}}, a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Dios y {{plural_you:Dios de ustedes|vuestro Dios}}”».
es.R: Jesús le dijo: «Ya no te aferres a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Todavía no he subido al Padre. Pero ve a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} {{gender:hermanos y hermanas|hermanos}} y diles esto: “Ahora subo a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre, que también es {{plural_you:el Padre de ustedes|vuestro Padre}}. Subo a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Dios, que también es {{plural_you:el Dios de ustedes|vuestro Dios}}”».

fr.L: Jésus lui dit : « Ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} retiens pas, car je ne suis pas encore monté vers le Père ; mais va vers {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} et dis-leur : “Je monte vers {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père et votre Père, et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu et votre Dieu.” »
fr.B: Jésus lui dit : « Cesse de {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} retenir, car je ne suis pas encore monté vers le Père. Va plutôt trouver {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} et dis-leur : “Je monte auprès de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père et de votre Père, de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu et de votre Dieu.” »
fr.R: Jésus lui a dit : « Ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} retiens plus. Je ne suis pas encore monté vers le Père. Mais va trouver {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} et dis-leur ceci : “Je monte vers {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père, qui est aussi votre Père. Je vais vers {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu, qui est aussi votre Dieu.” »

sw.B: Yesu akamwambia, "Usiendelee kunishikilia, kwa sababu bado sijapaa kwa Baba. Badala yake nenda kwa ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} na ujumbe huu: 'Ninapaa kwa Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na Baba yenu, kwa Mungu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} na Mungu wenu.'"
sw.R: Yesu akamwambia, "Usiendelee kunishikilia. Bado sijapanda juu kwa Baba. Lakini nenda kwa ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}, uwaambie hivi: 'Ninapanda juu kwa Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, ambaye ni Baba yenu pia. Ninakwenda kwa Mungu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, ambaye ni Mungu wenu pia.'"

Nhưng hãy đi đến với {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và nói với họ: 'Ta đang lên cùng Cha của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và Cha của các con, Đức Chúa Trời của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và Đức Chúa Trời của các con.'"

Nhưng hãy đi đến với {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và nói với họ: 'Ta đang lên cùng Cha của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, cũng là Cha của các con; cùng Đức Chúa Trời của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, cũng là Đức Chúa Trời của các con.'"
