Nhưng bà hãy đi đến với {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và nói với họ thế này: 'Ta sắp lên với Cha của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, cũng là Cha của các con. Ta lên với Đức Chúa Trời của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, cũng là Đức Chúa Trời của các con.'"

ko.L: 예수께서 그 여자에게 말씀하신다. "나를 붙잡지 마라. 내가 아직 아버지께 올라가지 않았기 때문이다. 그러나 내 {{gender:형제자매들|형제들}}에게 가서 그들에게 말하여라. '나는 내 아버지이시며 너희 아버지이신 분, 내 하나님이시며 너희 하나님이신 분께 올라간다.'"
ko.B: 예수께서 마리아에게 말씀하셨다. "더 이상 나를 붙들고 있지 마라. 내가 아직 아버지께 올라가지 않았다. 그 대신 내 {{gender:형제자매들|형제들}}에게 가서 이렇게 전하여라. '나는 나의 아버지이자 너희의 아버지, 나의 하나님이자 너희의 하나님이신 분께로 올라간다.'"
ko.R: 예수께서 마리아에게 말씀하셨다. "더 이상 나를 붙들고 있지 마라. 나는 아직 아버지께 올라가지 않았다. 내 {{gender:형제자매들|형제들}}에게 가서 이렇게 말해 주어라. '나는 내 아버지께 올라간다. 그분은 너희의 아버지도 되신다. 나는 내 하나님께 올라간다. 그분은 너희의 하나님도 되신다.'"

pt.L: Jesus lhe diz: "Não {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} segure, pois ainda não subi para o Pai; mas vá aos {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}} e diga a eles: 'Estou subindo para o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai e Pai de vocês, e {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Deus e Deus de vocês.'"
pt.B: Jesus lhe disse: "Pare de {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} segurar, porque ainda não subi para o Pai. Em vez disso, vá aos {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}} com esta mensagem: 'Estou subindo para o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai e Pai de vocês, para o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Deus e Deus de vocês.'"
pt.R: Jesus disse a ela: "Não fique {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} segurando. Eu ainda não subi para o Pai. Mas vá até os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}} e diga isto a eles: 'Eu estou subindo para o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai, que é também o Pai de vocês. Estou indo para o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Deus, que é também o Deus de vocês.'"

am.L: ኢየሱስ እንዲህ ይላታል፦ «አትያዢኝ፤ ገና ወደ አብ አላረግኩምና፤ ነገር ግን ወደ {{gender:ወንድሞቼና እኅቶቼ|ወንድሞቼ}} ሂጂና እንዲህ በያቸው፦ “ወደ አባቴና ወደ አባታችሁ፣ ወደ አምላኬና ወደ አምላካችሁ ዐርጋለሁ።”»
am.B: ኢየሱስም እንዲህ አላት፦ «ይዘሽ አታቆዪኝ፤ ገና ወደ አብ አላረግኩምና። ይልቅስ ወደ {{gender:ወንድሞቼና እኅቶቼ|ወንድሞቼ}} ሄደሽ ይህን መልእክት ንገሪያቸው፦ “ወደ አባቴ፣ ወደ አባታችሁም፣ ወደ አምላኬ፣ ወደ አምላካችሁም ዐርጋለሁ።”»
am.R: ኢየሱስም እንዲህ አላት፦ «ይዘሽ አታቆዪኝ። ገና ወደ አብ አልሄድኩም። ነገር ግን ወደ {{gender:ወንድሞቼና እኅቶቼ|ወንድሞቼ}} ሄደሽ እንዲህ በያቸው፦ “ወደ አባቴ እሄዳለሁ፤ እርሱ የእናንተም አባት ነው። ወደ አምላኬ እሄዳለሁ፤ እርሱ የእናንተም አምላክ ነው።”»

decisions.choice: do not hold on to me: stop clinging to me
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to touch, but also to take hold of and cling to. The command is in the present tense with "not", which most often tells someone to stop what they are already doing. Mary has taken hold of him, as the women do in Matthew 28:9, and he tells her not to keep holding him. Jesus is not forbidding any touch at all: a week later he invites Thomas to touch his wounds (20:27). The well-known rendering "Do not touch me" goes back to the older translations.

decisions.choice: for I have not yet ascended: he is not yet gone, and she need not hold him back
alternatives: she must not touch him until he has ascended and returned
she must not hold him back from ascending
decisions.reason: The reason is hard. It seems to mean that Jesus has not yet returned to the Father, so she does not need to cling to him as if he were about to vanish; there is time, and she has a message to carry. It may also mean that the old way of being with him is over: his going to the Father will bring a new kind of presence through the Spirit (14:18-19; 16:7, 22). John does not say more.

decisions.choice: my brothers: the disciples, the whole group of Jesus's followers
decisions.reason: Mary goes to "the disciples" (verse 18), so Jesus means his followers, not his brothers by birth (7:3-5). It is the first time he calls them his brothers: they now share his Father (the end of the verse; compare Matthew 28:10; Hebrews 2:11-12). The masculine plural covers a mixed group, and the followers gathered that evening (verse 19) were very likely women as well as men (compare Acts 1:14).

decisions.choice: my Father and your Father, my God and your God: a shared Father, yet named in two ways
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say "our Father". He is the Son in a way no one else is (1:14, 18), and those who believe in him become children of God through him (1:12). Through him his Father is now their Father, and his God their God (compare Ruth 1:16). The present "I am ascending" speaks of his return to the Father as already under way (13:1; 16:28).

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The brothers are the community of disciples, men and women (meaning decision m3), so the inclusive form is the default and "brothers" the alternative.

decisions.choice: Do not hold on to me (L); Do not keep holding on to me (B, R)
decisions.reason: Shows that he is telling her to stop clinging, not forbidding a touch (meaning decision m1); the footnote gives "Do not touch me".

decisions.choice: gone up, going up (R); ascended, ascending (L, B)
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for the ascent and spells out the shared Father and God in two short sentences.

decisions.choice: No me retengas (L); Deja de aferrarte a mí (B); Ya no te aferres a mí (R)
decisions.reason: Jesus tells her to stop clinging to him, not to avoid any touch (meaning decision m1). "Retener" is holding someone back; "aferrarse" is clinging. The footnote gives "No me toques", the familiar rendering.

decisions.choice: {{gender:hermanos y hermanas|hermanos}}; {{plural_you:Padre de ustedes|vuestro Padre}}
decisions.reason: The brothers are the community of disciples, men and women (meaning decision m3), so the inclusive form is the default. "Your" is plural: it takes the ustedes / vosotros setting, written "de ustedes" because "su Padre" could be read as "his Father". Every plural "you" in this passage takes the setting.

decisions.choice: Ne me retiens pas (L); Cesse de me retenir (B); Ne me retiens plus (R)
decisions.reason: The verb here means to take hold of and cling to, and the present tense with "not" tells her to stop what she is doing (meaning decision m1). "Retenir" says both holding and holding back, which fits the reason given (meaning decision m2). The familiar "Ne me touche pas" (Latin "Noli me tangere") is given in the footnote of the English decision.

decisions.choice: {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}; monter (every level)
decisions.reason: The brothers are the community of disciples, men and women (meaning decision m3), so the inclusive form is the default and "frères" the alternative, as in the English. French "monter" is already the plain verb for the ascent, so Readable needs no other word.

decisions.choice: ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English has a gender setting here, because the brothers are the whole community of disciples, men and women (meaning decision m3). Swahili "ndugu" already means brothers and sisters, and the only narrower form, "ndugu wa kiume", would change the meaning, so there is nothing for the setting to change. The possessive "zangu" takes the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: Usinishikilie (L); Usiendelee kunishikilia (B, R); kupaa (L, B); kupanda juu (R)
decisions.reason: "Kushikilia" is to hold on to, and Balanced and Readable add "usiendelee" (do not go on) for the present command with "not": he tells her to stop clinging, not that she may not touch him (meaning decision m1). "Usiniguse" (do not touch me) would say the second. "Kupaa" is the usual word for the ascension; Readable says plainly "go up".

decisions.choice: "các con" for "you" in the message to the disciples
decisions.reason: The message is Jesus speaking to his disciples, whom he calls "các con" (style guide section 6). Calling them his brothers and sisters does not change that address; the gender setting applies only to the noun "anh chị em / anh em".

decisions.choice: {{gender:형제자매들|형제들}}
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads "my brothers" as the whole group of Jesus's followers, which is where the style guide allows a gender span for adelphoi (section 7); the plural "-들" is kept in both forms.

decisions.choice: one Father and one God named twice: "내 아버지이시며 너희 아버지이신 분" (L); "나의 아버지이자 너희의 아버지" (B); two short sentences (R)
decisions.reason: "A와 B" in Korean would suggest two different persons; the Greek names one Father and one God in two ways (meaning decision). The wording also avoids the familiar older rendering.

decisions.choice: Não me segure (L); Pare de me segurar (B); Não fique me segurando (R)
decisions.reason: As the English, the wording says that she is to stop clinging to him, not that she may not touch him (meaning decision m1); Balanced and Readable bring out the present tense with "pare de" and "ficar ... -ndo". The footnote gives "Não me toque".

decisions.choice: {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}
decisions.reason: As the English (meaning decision m3): the disciples, men and women. The "eles" that follows is the ordinary Portuguese plural for a mixed group and needs no span.

decisions.choice: ወደ ወንድሞቼና እኅቶቼ by default; ወንድሞቼ as the alternative
decisions.reason: Jesus means the whole group of his followers, women among them, so the default says ወንድሞቼና እኅቶቼ (my brothers and sisters) and the setting gives the Greek's ወንድሞቼ.

decisions.choice: አትያዢኝ (L); ይዘሽ አታቆዪኝ (B, R) for "do not hold on to me"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the words as "stop clinging to me", not a ban on touching; ይዘሽ አታቆዪኝ (do not hold me back) says that, and Literal keeps the plain "do not hold me".

source.text: ἔρχεται Μαριὰμ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ ἀγγέλλουσα τοῖς μαθηταῖς ὅτι Ἑώρακα τὸν κύριον καὶ ταῦτα εἶπεν αὐτῇ.

records.literal_gloss: Comes Mariam the Magdalene announcing to the disciples, "I have seen the Lord," and these things he said to her.

en.L: Mary Magdalene comes, announcing to the disciples, "I have seen the Lord," and [that] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said these things to her.
en.B: Mary Magdalene went and brought the disciples the news: "I have seen the Lord!" And she reported to them what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said to her.
en.R: So Mary Magdalene went to the disciples with the news: "I have seen the Lord!" She also told them what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said to her.

es.L: Viene María Magdalena anunciando a los discípulos: «He visto al Señor», y [que] {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le había dicho estas cosas.
es.B: María Magdalena fue a dar la noticia a los discípulos: «¡He visto al Señor!». Y les contó lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le había dicho.
es.R: Entonces María Magdalena fue a los discípulos con la noticia: «¡He visto al Señor!». También les contó lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le había dicho.

fr.L: Marie de Magdala vient annoncer aux disciples : « J’ai vu le Seigneur », et [que] {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui avait dit ces choses.
fr.B: Marie de Magdala alla porter la nouvelle aux disciples : « J’ai vu le Seigneur ! » Et elle leur rapporta ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui avait dit.
fr.R: Alors Marie de Magdala est allée annoncer la nouvelle aux disciples : « J’ai vu le Seigneur ! » Elle leur a aussi raconté ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui avait dit.

sw.L: Mariamu Magdalene anakuja akiwatangazia wanafunzi, "Nimemwona Bwana," na [kwamba] alimwambia mambo hayo.
sw.B: Mariamu Magdalene alikwenda, akawaletea wanafunzi habari: "Nimemwona Bwana!" Akawaeleza mambo aliyoambiwa {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Mariamu Magdalene alikwenda kwa wanafunzi na habari hii: "Nimemwona Bwana!" Aliwaeleza pia yale ambayo Yesu alikuwa amemwambia.

vi.L: Ma-ri Ma-đơ-len đến báo cho các môn đồ: "Tôi đã thấy Chúa," và [rằng] {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nói với bà những điều ấy.
vi.B: Ma-ri Ma-đơ-len đi báo tin cho các môn đồ: "Tôi đã thấy Chúa!" Bà cũng thuật lại cho họ những điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nói với bà.
vi.R: Vậy Ma-ri Ma-đơ-len đến báo tin cho các môn đồ: "Tôi đã thấy Chúa!" Bà cũng kể cho họ những gì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nói với bà.

ko.L: 막달라 마리아가 와서 제자들에게 알린다. "제가 주님을 뵈었어요!" 그리고 그분이 자기에게 이것들을 말씀하셨다고 [전했다].
ko.B: 막달라 마리아는 제자들에게 가서 "제가 주님을 뵈었어요!" 하고 소식을 전했다. 그리고 주님께서 자기에게 하신 말씀도 전했다.
ko.R: 그래서 막달라 마리아는 제자들에게 가서 소식을 알렸다. "제가 주님을 뵈었어요!" 그리고 주님께서 자기에게 하신 말씀도 전해 주었다.

pt.L: Maria Madalena vem anunciando aos discípulos: "Eu vi o Senhor", e [que] {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhe tinha dito essas coisas.

decisions.choice: announcing: bringing news as a messenger
decisions.reason: The verb belongs to the same family as the word for messenger, or angel. Mary, sent by Jesus (verse 17), is the first to bring the news that he is risen.

decisions.choice: I have seen the Lord: the first witness to the risen Jesus
decisions.reason: The perfect tense speaks of a seeing that has lasting effect. The disciples will say the same words to Thomas (20:25). "The Lord" is now the risen Jesus.

decisions.choice: a quotation, then a report of what he said
decisions.reason: The sentence moves from her own words ("I have seen") to reported speech ("he had said these things to her"). Greek moves between the two freely.

decisions.choice: [that] (L); she reported to them what (B); She also told them what (R)
alternatives: and he said these things to her
decisions.reason: English needs a verb or a linking word for the change to reported speech (meaning decision m3). Literal shows the supplied word in brackets.

decisions.choice: [que] (L); les contó lo que (B, R)
alternatives: y él le dijo estas cosas
decisions.reason: As in English: Spanish needs a linking word or a verb for the change from her own words to reported speech (meaning decision m3). The stressed "él" is Jesus and takes the setting.

decisions.choice: annoncer (every level); et [que] (L); elle leur rapporta ce que (B); Elle leur a aussi raconté ce que (R)
decisions.reason: "Annoncer" is the verb of a messenger bringing news (meaning decision m1). The sentence moves from her own words to reported speech (meaning decision m3); French needs a link, bracketed at Literal, or a verb of reporting.

decisions.choice: mambo aliyoambiwa naye (what she was told by him) (B); yale ambayo Yesu alikuwa amemwambia (R)
decisions.reason: The Swahili subject prefix a- does not tell "he" from "she", so "aliyokuwa amemwambia" could mean what Mary had said. Balanced uses the passive with "naye" (by him), which takes the deity_pronoun setting; Readable names Jesus. Literal keeps the Greek wording.
